subject.title: [Feature]: Add bounded/validated append semantics for pre-compaction memory flush

question: Should OpenClaw accept a strict built-in daily-memory append guard for memory-flush writes now, or wait for a broader configurable validation/hook design?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested runtime contract, and the remaining choice affects default fail-closed behavior plus a possible security-sensitive validation API.

options.title: Land the narrow built-in guard
options.body: Rebase and review the linked candidate path so canonical daily-memory flush writes are bounded, scaffold-filtered, deduped, and telemetry-backed without adding shell hooks.

options.title: Design a typed validation API first
options.body: Pause the fix until maintainers define a plugin or config contract for validation, rollback, and security boundaries.

options.title: Defer to broader memory tooling
options.body: Keep this issue open under a larger memory-tool design, accepting that the current raw append boundary remains unchanged for now.

recommendation.title: Land the narrow built-in guard
recommendation.body: Rebase and review the linked candidate path so canonical daily-memory flush writes are bounded, scaffold-filtered, deduped, and telemetry-backed without adding shell hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about core runtime policy and security/config shape, and Peter has recent adjacent compaction and source-split history.
